title: Knowledge check: Advanced Reactivity Utilities

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Advanced Reactivity Utilities”?
options: Refs in script do not use .value.
Destructuring always preserves reactive tracking automatically.
Use computed() for pure derived values and watchers for side effects caused by reactive changes.
A computed getter should send network requests every time it is evaluated.
questions.answer_key: Use computed() for pure derived values and watchers for side effects caused by reactive changes.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Advanced Reactivity Utilities directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “toRef() and toRefs()”, which practice is most reliable?
options: A ref cannot hold a primitive value.
Use ref() to create a reactive reference; update its .value in JavaScript and use the ref directly in the template.
A ref must be updated by manually changing innerHTML.
Use ref().value in every Vue template expression.
questions.answer_key: Use ref() to create a reactive reference; update its .value in JavaScript and use the ref directly in the template.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “toRef() and toRefs()”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Advanced Reactivity Utilities” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
